description: BESOS is a Python library for simulating and optimising buildings and urban energy systems, built to help researchers and practitioners design more sustainable, district-integrated buildings. It was developed by Ralph Evins's Energy In Cities group at the University of Victoria, Canada. It wraps the EnergyPlus building simulator and the EnergyHub district energy model, runs large parametric analyses with results in pandas DataFrames, fits machine-learning surrogate models with scikit-learn and other libraries, and couples them to optimisation algorithms. Coverage: any building or district that can be modelled in EnergyPlus or EnergyHub. Access: source on GitLab, releases on PyPI (latest 2.2.3, uploaded 31 May 2024) and an archived v2.1.3 on Zenodo. Licence: GNU General Public License v2; free. Caveats: no release since mid-2024, and simulations need EnergyPlus installed. Simulation uses are building design and retrofit optimisation, surrogate models for fast urban energy scenarios, and district energy system sizing. Related records: EnergyPlus and archetypal.
